expectations.text: Output contains all five platform sections: YouTube Description, LinkedIn Post, Instagram Caption, TikTok Caption, and Twitter/X
expectations.evidence: All five platform sections present: YOUTUBE DESCRIPTION, INSTAGRAM CAPTION, LINKEDIN CAPTION, TIKTOK CAPTION, TWITTER / X.

expectations.text: LinkedIn post opens with a strong hook (question, bold claim, or surprising stat) — not a generic opener like 'In this video'
expectations.evidence: 'I've seen it happen over and over: a sales leader buys an AI tool, rolls it out to the team, and 6 months later nobody's using it.' — story-based hook, not generic.

expectations.text: LinkedIn post includes a soft CTA rather than aggressive sales language
expectations.evidence: 'What's been your experience with AI tool adoption in sales? Drop a comment below.' — conversational engagement CTA, not salesy.

expectations.text: TikTok caption includes a trending sound suggestion
expectations.evidence: No trending sound suggestion included in the TikTok section. Baseline Claude doesn't know to include this.

expectations.text: At least 2 of these hashtags appear: #SalesAI #GTM #AIAutomation #AITools #FutureOfWork #AutomationNation
expectations.evidence: #SalesAI, #GTM, #FutureOfWork appear in the LinkedIn and Twitter sections.

expectations.text: No competitor tool names are mentioned
expectations.evidence: No specific competitor tools named. References to 'AI tools' are generic.

expectations.text: The core insight ('reps have to win first') is reflected in at least one platform's caption
expectations.evidence: Twitter: 'Win the rep first. Make the AI serve them.' LinkedIn: 'the reps have to win first' implied through narrative. Core insight present.

expectations.text: Each platform section uses the correct structural separator (━━━ dividers) as specified in the skill
expectations.evidence: Uses plain text headers (YOUTUBE DESCRIPTION, INSTAGRAM CAPTION, etc.) with no separator lines. Not the ━━━ format specified in the skill.
